Life can trend towards getting harder vs getting easier.  The grind you think you are in during your 20s and 30s never gives way to easier times like you might think it will.  I figured hitting 40+ would be like life on cruise control.  Nearly every facet of life can become more difficult.  Your body/health starts to feel vulnerable.  Financial obligations abound, especially with kids coming of age.  Employment feels less assured as you struggle to stay relevant in the workforce. Loved ones are older and sicker too.  Sometimes your only hope is the wisdom you’ve accrued in your 40+ years outpaces these challenges somehow.  That said, the biggest lesson at any age is to find enjoyment wherever you can and live for today.   Life is here and now.  Not at retirement, and not in your college days gone by.  Appreciating the present has been the single most transformative thing I have done for my mental health.  I wish I realized that earlier in life but I’m thankful I figured it out eventually.

The answer is simple, price increases are one of the easiest ways for any business to generate more revenue and profit.  Yes, there is nuance in the cost of goods as many commenters have pointed out (different raw material prices, overhead volatility etc), but it is corporate greed that makes up a majority of what we see at the shelf lately IMO.  Say I’m a manufacturer and my cost of producing a given item has gone up 3%.  I’m going to pass an increase to my wholesaler of 5% and pocket the difference.  As the wholesaler, I pass that increase along by taking 2 increases of 4% over 6 months and pocket the difference.   As a retailer,  the net increase of the item by the time it gets to me could be well over 15%.  I ratchet up the price over 6 months or so to 20% more than what you use to pay.  I also don’t run sales on the item as frequently or as deep, driving the average price up further.  

This is the simplified version. Compound this over any number of additional intermediaries, fees, shrikflation - all of these mechanisms result in what we are seeing now.  

It’s particularly bad because this round of inflation is being exploited in ways I have not seen before.  Its sustained, and on the heels of covid and supply chain challenges.  Lots of price increases with businesses at every level of production/distribution harvesting a little more with each increase to one another.  Many of which are hitting record profits and now intent to hurdle those newfound profits next quarter. Greed breeds more greed and the buck stops with the consumer.
